meta.unit: index (2010 = 100) for the path; percentage points for the rate
meta.method_note: Every model is backtested with rolling-origin, expanding-window folds. Nothing is trained on data that would not have been available at the time.

series.label: All items (headline)
series.verdict: ets beat the persistence baseline on the backtest (MAE 0.17pp vs 0.46pp over 96 forecasts).
caveats: Backtests are rolling-origin and expanding-window: each fold fits only on data available at that time.
Accuracy is measured on the year-on-year inflation rate in percentage points, not on the index level. Scoring on the index would flatter every model, since the index only goes up.

The baseline is persistence of the inflation rate (last year's rate), not the textbook seasonal-naive index baseline -- under year-on-year scoring that one predicts exactly 0% inflation by construction and would be a straw man.
